challenge.title: Social and Cultural Evidence Challenge
challenge.description: Complete 10 activities: five clue-and-conclusion decisions and five matching tasks. Both parts of an evidence decision count together as one activity. Get at least 7 activities correct. Every supplied clue is available without saving it in your journal.

badge.name: Social and Cultural Investigator
badge.description: Earned by completing all five Chapter 10 missions and passing the evidence challenge. Recognizes careful explanations of housing, learning, social experience, cultural works, continuity and change.

evidence.question: A town founding date is attached to every visible house feature. Which clue directly checks that claim?
choices: Settlement beginnings, construction, alteration and repair may have different dates
Every house feature must date to the towns founding
Looking old establishes an exact date
One photograph records every earlier appearance
evidence.explanation: Date particular building stages separately. A towns beginning does not date every later feature.

evidence.question: A printed teaching book is used to claim every person accepted its teaching. Which clue directly checks this?
choices: A printed book does not establish every persons reading, understanding or belief
Publication guarantees universal acceptance
Everyone necessarily read the same copy
Every earlier tradition disappeared immediately
evidence.explanation: A dated material is evidence of production. Circulation, learning and belief need appropriate further evidence.

evidence.question: A social-category label is used to decide a persons wealth and occupation. Which clue directly checks this leap?
choices: A category alone does not establish wealth, occupation or every experience
Every person in a category had identical income
A label reveals every private motive
A category is a measure of intelligence
evidence.explanation: Investigate particular lives and conditions. A source category is not a complete biography or measure of human worth.

evidence.question: A caption dates the Basi Revolt paintings to 1807 because they show that event. Which clue supplies the making date?
choices: The Museum dates the painting series to 1821 and attributes it to Villanueva
Every depiction shares its events date
The images are photographs taken during the event
A later exhibition date must be the making date
evidence.explanation: Separate the 1807 event and the 1821 painting series. Depiction and event are different stages.

evidence.question: A petition is used to claim people had unlimited freedom and guaranteed success. Which clue directly checks that claim about agency?
choices: Agency does not mean equal power, unlimited choice or automatic success
Every request automatically succeeded
Everyone had equal power
A category determines every response
evidence.explanation: People could act within constraints. Check the request and its documented outcome separately.

matching.question: Match each housing source with the question it helps investigate.
pairs: What the building parts were made from
Which activities were recorded in a space
What features and changes were documented during repair
matching.explanation: Materials, use and later repair answer different questions. A model or modern record is not every earlier households complete story.

matching.question: Match these learning-history ideas with their meanings.
pairs: An object or text used to communicate a lesson
A practical opportunity to reach and take part
matching.explanation: A material or translation does not guarantee access, identical understanding or acceptance. Historical religious inquiry does not assess personal faith.

matching.question: Match these social-experience ideas with their careful descriptions.
pairs: An arrangement of unequal power and privileges
A role rather than proof of every action
A formal request rather than automatic success
matching.explanation: Use evidence for actual conduct and outcomes. Categories and privileges do not measure human worth.

matching.question: Match these cultural-history questions with the evidence to seek.
pairs: Who requested work and who carried it out
Why a record or work was produced or used
matching.explanation: Keep makers, dates and purposes distinct. A later depiction or display is not automatically an original eyewitness record.

matching.question: Match each comparison idea with its meaning.
pairs: Something carrying on during other changes
Putting a plan or rule into practice
Peoples ability to act within conditions and limits
matching.explanation: Change and continuity can coexist. Policies and peoples actions need evidence of actual conditions and outcomes.
